task_description: Predicting C–H dissociation energy barriers for transition metal single-atom alloy (SAA) surfaces to identify high-activity catalysts for methane cracking, enabling rapid screening of optimal SAA compositions from a vast candidate space before experimental validation.

datasets.db_title: DFT-computed C–H dissociation energy barriers for 623 SAA surfaces
datasets.db_description: A dataset of 623 density functional theory (DFT)-computed C–H dissociation energy barriers across diverse transition metal single-atom alloy (SAA) surfaces, covering various host metals (e.g., Fe, Co, Ni) and dopant atoms (e.g., Ir, Re, Ru). This dataset was used to train and validate the machine learning regression model for predicting C–H dissociation barriers — the key activity descriptor for methane cracking — and to establish structure–property relationships guiding catalyst selection.

datasets.db_title: Automated SAA surface database of 10,950 entries
datasets.db_description: A computationally generated database containing 10,950 distinct transition metal single-atom alloy (SAA) surface configurations, constructed by substituting a single host atom in the top surface layer with a dopant atom. Each entry includes structural and electronic descriptors (e.g., doped_weighted_surface_energy, com_top_d_e_number, host_surface_energy). This database served as the candidate space for ML-based screening: the trained ML model predicted C–H dissociation barriers across all 10,950 surfaces to prioritize top-performing SAAs (e.g., Ir/Ni, Re/Ni) for experimental synthesis and testing.
